OAuth app readiness guide · Docs and knowledge

Getting your Confluence app ready for real users

Tested in a real setup attemptChecked 2026-10-28atlassian.com/software/confluence

Verdict. A private Atlassian OAuth app takes about 5 minutes and no review. Sharing it with customers is self-serve but needs vendor details, policy links and a personal data declaration. For an agent that stores or caches Confluence data, that declaration brings reporting obligations.

01

At a glance

The answer in one screen
Ease of creation
Easy
About 5 minutes in our test, across three console pages.
Ease of approval
Self-serve
No review to share an OAuth app. Marketplace listing is separate.
Your hands-on time
15 min to 1 day
Minutes for the app; longer if you need a privacy policy and a personal data reporting setup.
Waiting on the provider
None
Sharing takes effect when you save it.
Do you need your own app yet?
Check Composio first.
We could not confirm a Composio-managed Atlassian app.
Watch out: decisions you can't undo
  • Access type is set at creation. Pick Resource-level unless your agent truly needs every site.
  • The personal data answer is almost always Yes for agents. Decide your caching and memory design before you share, and plan for the Personal data reporting API.
  • Stopping sharing affects existing users. Share only when ready to support customers.
Agent an agent can do it You needs you Waiting on the provider
02

Prerequisites

What to have ready

To create and connect

  • An Atlassian account; agreement to Atlassian's developer terms
  • The Composio callback URL (up to 30 callback URLs allowed)

For approval (can take days)

  • Vendor name, privacy policy URL, terms of service URL, support contact
  • A personal data decision, and Personal data reporting API handling if Yes
03

Which one is right for an agent product?

The default after creation.
Who can install
Only you
Review
None
Use it for
Building and testing
Recommended for agents

After providing vendor and security details.
Who can install
Anyone with your authorization URL
Review
None

Forge app

Created as a Forge app instead.
Who can install
Installed into sites by admins
Review
Marketplace for distribution
Use it for
Apps that run inside Atlassian
Classic vs granular scopesAtlassian has two scope systems. After adding only classic scopes, the console warned that the Confluence API had no granular scopes. Newer endpoints need granular scopes; mixing them up is a common cause of 401 errors. Tested
04

Creation steps

Who does what, and how long it takes
  1. YouSign in to developer.atlassian.com
    1 min
    Console, My apps. A new Developer Space selector may appear.
  2. AgentCreate, OAuth 2.0 integration
    1 min
    Name the app and choose Resource-level access.
  3. YouAgree to developer terms and create
    5 sec
    The page notes rotating refresh tokens are mandatory for new apps.
  4. AgentAdd the Confluence API and scopes
    2 min
    Permissions, Confluence API, Configure, Edit scopes. Choose classic or granular per the endpoints you call.
  5. AgentAdd OAuth 2.0 (3LO) and the callback
    1 min
    Authorization page, then paste the Composio callback. The page then generates an authorization URL.
  6. YouFill distribution details and share
    15 min
    Vendor name, policy links, support contact, personal data answer, then switch to Sharing.
  7. YouCopy credentials into Composio
    2 min
    From the app's Settings page.

In our test: about 5 minutes to a private app with scopes and callback. Sharing was not switched on (needs real policy URLs).

05

Scopes

What each permission costs you

Scopes are added per API (Confluence, Jira, User identity, Personal data reporting and more). Atlassian recommends no more than 50 scopes in total.

Agent use caseScopesWhat it costs you
Search pages and spacessearch:confluenceClassic scope
Read content summariesread:confluence-content.summaryread:confluence-space.summaryClassic scopes
Read full page bodiesread:confluence-content.allClassic scope
Create and edit pageswrite:confluence-contentClassic scope
Newer v2 endpointsgranular scopes (e.g. read:page:confluence)Required by many newer endpoints
Keep refreshing without the useroffline_accessNeeded for refresh tokens
Minimal set: "Answer from our wiki" agentsearch:confluenceread:confluence-content.alloffline_access
Check each endpoint's docs for whether it wants granular scopes.

Changing scopes later

  • Edit scopes on the Permissions page; users must reauthorize to grant new ones.
  • No review for OAuth apps.
06

Approval and distribution

Review, cost and renewal

When you need it: No review to share an OAuth 2.0 app. Atlassian Marketplace listing is a separate path. Cost: None to share. Renewal: If you declared personal data: ongoing reporting through the Personal data reporting API.

Share
Immediate
Self-serve, once details are saved.

What you submit

  • Vendor and security details
  • Personal data declaration

Common rejection reasons

  • Not applicable for sharing

Before approval: what works and what's capped

Build and test
Private app, only you.
Limit: Customers cannot authorize until Sharing is on.
First customers
Shared app, any site via your URL.
Limit: Resource-level apps see only the site the user picked.
Scale
Same app.
Limit: Rate limit tier shown on the app; reporting duties if you store personal data.
07

Data use and compliance

Rules that shape agent design
  • Personal data declaration. Yes if you store personal data with account IDs or cache data longer than 24 hours.
  • Personal data reporting. Apps that store personal data report the accounts they hold, so deleted or changed users can be handled.
Design impactAgent memory or a vector index of Confluence pages counts as storing data. Decide this before you share. Tested

SymptomCauseFix

OAuth app readiness guide · Email

Getting your Gmail app ready for real users

Tested in a real setup attemptChecked 2026-10-28gmail.com

Verdict. The scope you pick decides the project. Sending mail needs a short verification. Reading mail means restricted-scope review plus a paid security assessment renewed every year. Until verified, your app is capped at 100 users for its lifetime and test tokens die after 7 days.

01

At a glance

The answer in one screen
Ease of creation
Moderate
About 10 minutes to a Testing-mode app in our test.
Ease of approval
Very hard (read)
Read access needs verification plus a CASA security assessment. Send-only is moderate.
Your hands-on time
1 to 3 days
Domain verification, privacy policy, demo video, scope justifications. Plus assessor work for read access.
Waiting on the provider
Days to 6 weeks
Brand check 2 to 3 business days; sensitive scopes under a week; restricted scopes plus CASA several weeks.
Do you need your own app yet?
Start on Composio's managed Gmail app.
It skips verification for you, but users see Composio on Google's consent screen, scopes are fixed (full mailbox in Composio's own test) and quota is shared. Move to your own app when branding or narrow scopes matter.
Watch out: decisions you can't undo
  • The 100-user cap counts for the app's lifetime. Use a separate Google Cloud project for development and testing so you do not burn your production project's 100 users.
  • "Internal" is only for Google Workspace organizations. Solo developers and startups without Workspace should plan for verification from day one.
  • Uploading a logo triggers verification. Skip the logo until you are ready to submit.
  • Adding a restricted scope later means a new assessment. Pick your restricted scopes once, before the assessment.
Agent an agent can do it You needs you Waiting on the provider
02

Prerequisites

What to have ready

To create and connect

  • A Google account and a new Google Cloud project (separate one for testing)
  • User support email: your account or a Google Group you manage (a shared inbox must be a Group)
  • Agreement to the Google API Services User Data Policy

For approval (can take days)

  • Public homepage and privacy policy on the same domain, linked from the consent screen
  • Domain ownership verified in Google Search Console
  • Unlisted YouTube demo video showing the consent screen, client ID and each scope in use
  • Scope justifications naming the feature and why narrower scopes won't work
  • Restricted scopes: a CASA assessment through an authorized assessor (reported cost about $540 to $3,000+)
03

Composio's managed app is a valid launch pathMany teams launch on Composio's verified Gmail app and move to their own once the product is proven. You trade branding, scope control and dedicated quota for skipping the review. Secondary source
04

Creation steps

Who does what, and how long it takes
  1. YouSign in and create a project
    1 min
    console.cloud.google.com. The console may stay on another project until you switch.
  2. AgentRun the Google Auth Platform setup
    4 min
    App name, support email, audience (External), contact email.
  3. YouAgree to the User Data Policy and create
    10 sec
    Configuration is created in Testing status.
  4. AgentAdd scopes under Data Access
    3 min
    Gmail scopes only appear once the Gmail API is enabled; otherwise paste them in "Manually add scopes".
  5. AgentCreate an OAuth client
    2 min
    Web application, with the Composio callback as the redirect URI.
  6. YouVerify your domain
    30 min to 1 day
    In Google Search Console, with DNS or site access. An agent cannot do this for you.
  7. YouComplete Branding and record the video
    2 to 4 hours
    Homepage, privacy policy, terms, authorized domains, demo video.
  8. WaitingBrand and data access verification
    Days
    Brand check 2 to 3 business days. Sensitive scopes typically under a week.
  9. YouCASA assessment (restricted scopes only)
    5 to 20 days
    Scan, fix findings, answer the questionnaire, respond daily.

In our test: about 10 minutes to a Testing-mode app with Gmail scopes and three approvals. Production needs the human-only steps above.

05

Scopes

What each permission costs you

Google classifies every scope as non-sensitive, sensitive or restricted. The console sorted our scopes into these groups for us.

Agent use caseScopesWhat it costs you
Manage labels onlygmail.labelsNon-sensitive: brand check only
Send email on the user's behalfgmail.sendSensitive: verification, no CASA
Read messages and settingsgmail.readonlyRestricted: verification + CASA yearly
Read headers onlygmail.metadataRestricted too, despite sounding light
Drafts, modify, labels on mailgmail.composegmail.modifyRestricted
Full mailboxhttps://mail.google.com/Restricted; hardest to justify
Minimal set: "Send follow-ups" agentgmail.send
Avoids CASA entirely.
Minimal set: "Triage my inbox" agentgmail.readonlygmail.send
Restricted: budget for CASA and several weeks.

Changing scopes later

  • Adding a sensitive scope means re-verification.
  • Adding a restricted scope means re-verification and possibly a new security assessment.
  • Users can grant only some scopes (granular consent). Check granted scopes after every connection.
06

Approval and distribution

Review, cost and renewal

When you need it: Before any user outside your test list, and before your 100th user ever. Cost: Verification is free. CASA through an assessor: reported about $540 to $3,000+ per year. Renewal: Restricted scopes: CASA at least every 12 months. Google emails about 90 days before expiry.

Brand
2 to 3 business days
Publish within 7 days of a compliant result.
Sensitive
Under a week
Typical for send-only.
Restricted
Several weeks
Google says several weeks; prepared teams report 5 to 20 days.
CASA
5 to 20 days
With an authorized assessor, then a Letter of Assessment.

What you submit

  • Homepage, privacy policy, verified domain
  • Demo video
  • Scope justifications
  • CASA results for restricted scopes

Common rejection reasons

  • Requesting scopes you don't use
  • Video not showing each scope
  • Privacy policy missing Limited Use language
  • Unmonitored contact email

Replying to Google and your assessor quickly is the biggest lever on time.

Before approval: what works and what's capped

Build and test
Testing mode, listed test users.
Limit: 100 users for the app's lifetime; refresh tokens expire after 7 days; "unverified app" screen.
First customers
Composio's managed app, or your app once verified.
Limit: Your own unverified app is not usable for customers.
Scale
Verified app.
Limit: Restricted scopes: yearly CASA renewal.
The 7-day trapIn Testing, refresh tokens expire after 7 days. An agent that works in your demo will silently disconnect a week later. Secondary source
07

Data use and compliance

Rules that shape agent design
  • Limited Use. Google user data may only be used to provide or improve user-facing features.
  • No general model training on Workspace data. Disclose any AI use in the product and the privacy policy.
  • Security assessment is required when restricted-scope data can be reached from or through your servers.
Design impactIf your agent reads mail, budget for CASA, a yearly renewal and an AI-use disclosure. Official docs
08

Symptom, cause, fix
SymptomCauseFix
"Google hasn't verified this app" screenTesting mode or unverified production appComplete verification, or use Composio's managed app
Users disconnected after a weekTesting-mode refresh tokens expire after 7 daysMove to production and verify
Gmail scopes missing in the pickerGmail API not enabledEnable the API or paste the scope URLs manually
Cannot pick InternalNo Google Workspace organizationUse External and plan for verification
Review stallsContact inbox not monitoredUse a monitored Google Group and add a second project editor

OAuth app readiness guide · Project management

Getting your Linear app ready for real users

Tested in a real setup attemptChecked 2026-10-28linear.app

Verdict. The easiest app in the library: a public OAuth app in about 4 minutes, no review, no install cap. The one trap is that new apps are private by default, so your first customer cannot connect unless you switch on "Public".

01

At a glance

The answer in one screen
Ease of creation
Easy
About 4 minutes in our test, plus workspace onboarding if the workspace is new.
Ease of approval
None
No review. Public availability was immediate.
Your hands-on time
5 to 15 min
Form, redirect URL, one toggle. A new workspace adds a short onboarding.
Waiting on the provider
None
Nothing to wait for.
Do you need your own app yet?
Check Composio first; your own app is cheap here.
We could not confirm a Composio-managed Linear app. Since your own app takes minutes and needs no review, bringing your own is low cost.
Watch out: decisions you can't undo
  • New apps are private by default. Turn on Public before you share an install link with anyone. A Developer URL is required for public apps and is shown to users.
  • The workspace that owns the app sees its secret. Create the app in a dedicated workspace with few admins.
  • Refresh tokens rotate. Store the newest refresh token every time. All apps were moved to this system on April 1, 2026.
Agent an agent can do it You needs you Waiting on the provider
02

Prerequisites

What to have ready

To create and connect

  • A Linear workspace to own the app (ideally dedicated, few admins)
  • A Developer URL (homepage or docs page). Required for public apps
  • The Composio callback URL from your auth config

For approval (can take days)

  • Nothing. There is no review.

Act as the app, not the userAdd actor=app to the authorize URL so issues and comments are attributed to your agent instead of the person who connected. Linear's consent screen then shows the app as the actor. Official docs
04

Creation steps

Who does what, and how long it takes
  1. YouSign in and finish onboarding
    1 to 2 min
    In a brand-new workspace, onboarding ("Set up your profile") blocks Settings until it is done. Linear links may open the desktop app; choose "Open here instead".
  2. AgentOpen Settings, API, New application
    30 sec
    Path: /settings/api/applications/new in your workspace.
  3. AgentFill the form
    2 min
    Application name, developer name, Developer URL, description, redirect URI. All are shown to users at consent.
  4. AgentTurn on Public
    5 sec
    Off by default. Leave client credentials and webhooks off unless you need them.
  5. YouApprove Create
    5 sec
    The app is created instantly with "Availability: Publicly available". Client ID is shown; the secret is masked.
  6. YouCopy credentials into Composio
    2 min
    Create a custom auth config for the linear toolkit with the scopes from section 4.
  7. YouTest from a second workspace
    5 min
    Check the consent screen, including the team-access choice users will see.

Total in our test: about 4 minutes of agent work, onboarding and one approval.

05

Scopes

What each permission costs you

Linear has no scopes on the app itself. You request them in the authorize URL, so changing scopes means changing your Composio auth config, not the app.

Agent use caseScopesWhat it costs you
Read issues, projects, teamsreadAlways included
Create issues and attachmentsissues:createNo review
Comment on issuescomments:createNo review
Broad editswriteNo review, but users see broad access
Admin endpointsadminOnly when essential; scares admins at consent
Minimal set: "Triage bot" agentreadissues:createcomments:create
Narrower than write, and reads better on the consent screen.

Changing scopes later

  • Scopes live in the authorize URL, so update the Composio auth config and ask users to reconnect.
  • No re-review, because there is no review.
  • Requesting different scopes for client credentials revokes the existing app tokens.
06

Approval and distribution

Review, cost and renewal

When you need it: Never for OAuth. Linear's integrations directory listing is a separate, optional step. Cost: None. Renewal: None.

Review
None
Public apps work immediately.

What you submit

  • Nothing for OAuth

Common rejection reasons

  • Not applicable

Before approval: what works and what's capped

Build and test
Private app in your workspace.
Limit: Other workspaces cannot connect until Public is on.
First customers
Public app, any workspace.
Limit: Users may grant access to only some teams.
Scale
Same app.
Limit: Standard API rate limits only.
Users choose which teams you seeThe consent screen offers "All public teams" or "Only select teams". Private teams are not in "All public teams". An agent may see fewer issues than the user expects. Tested
07

Data use and compliance

Rules that shape agent design
  • Your terms apply. Linear's consent screen tells users that your app's use of their data is governed by your own terms and privacy policy, not Linear's.
  • Revocable by admins. Workspace owners and admins can revoke the connection at any time in Settings.
Design impactPublish a privacy policy before your first customer, and handle revoked tokens gracefully. Tested

SymptomCauseFix

Agent cannot see some issuesUser picked "Only select teams" or the issues are in private teamsAsk the user to reconnect and include those teams

Getting your Notion app ready for real users

Tested in a real setup attemptChecked 2026-10-28notion.com

Verdict. A working OAuth connection in about 4 minutes, no review. The trap is the very first choice: Notion defaults to a single-workspace API token, and the install scope you pick for OAuth is locked once the connection is created.

01

At a glance

The answer in one screen
Ease of creation
Easy
About 4 minutes in our test.
Ease of approval
None for OAuth
Marketplace listing is optional and separate.
Your hands-on time
10 to 20 min
Form, capabilities, then a page-sharing hint for your users.
Waiting on the provider
None
Nothing to wait for unless you list on the Marketplace.
Do you need your own app yet?
Check Composio first; your own connection is cheap here.
We could not confirm a Composio-managed Notion app. Your own connection needs no review.
Watch out: decisions you can't undo
  • API token is the default authentication method. Choose "OAuth" for any agent your customers will connect.
  • Install scope is locked after creation. Keep "Any workspace". Use a separate connection for internal testing if needed.
  • Deleting a connection revokes everyone. Never delete a live connection to "start fresh"; create a new one alongside.
Agent an agent can do it You needs you Waiting on the provider
02

Prerequisites

What to have ready

To create and connect

  • A Notion workspace (it becomes the connection's development workspace)
  • An HTTPS redirect URI with no fragments, wildcards, relative paths or public IP addresses
  • Agreement to Notion's Developer Terms (accepted when you create)

For approval (can take days)

  • Only for a Marketplace listing: listing content and images, managed under Listings
03

App types

Which one is right for an agent product?

API token connection

The default choice in the form.
Who can install
One workspace, shared token
Review
None
Use it for
Internal scripts and your own workspace
Recommended for agents

OAuth connection, any workspace

OAuth + Installable in: Any workspace.
Who can install
Any Notion user, each authorizes individually
Review
None
Use it for
Agent products with customers

OAuth, selected workspaces

OAuth + specific workspaces.
Who can install
Only workspaces you pick at creation
Review
None
Use it for
Pilots with named customers; not Marketplace-eligible
Integrations are now "Connections"The developer area moved to app.notion.com/developers under "Developer tools", with Connections, Workers, Personal access tokens and MCP tokens. Older guides point to notion.so/my-integrations. Tested
04

Creation steps

Who does what, and how long it takes
  1. YouSign in to Notion
    1 min
    Then open Developer tools, Connections. notion.so/profile/integrations redirects there.
  2. AgentNew connection, name it
    30 sec
    Name is shown to users.
  3. AgentSwitch authentication to OAuth
    5 sec
    The form defaults to API token (decision 1).
  4. AgentKeep Installable in: Any workspace
    5 sec
    Locked after creation (decision 2).
  5. AgentAdd the redirect URI
    1 min
    Pick the typed value from the suggestion list or it is not saved. This tripped our agent once.
  6. YouApprove Create connection
    5 sec
    This also accepts Notion's Developer Terms.
  7. AgentNarrow capabilities
    1 min
    Defaults include update, insert and reading user emails. Turn off what your agent does not need.
  8. YouCopy credentials into Composio
    2 min
    Client ID and secret from the Configuration tab. A ready-made authorization URL is shown too.

Total in our test: about 4 minutes of agent work and one approval.

05

Scopes

What each permission costs you

Notion uses capabilities set on the connection, not OAuth scope strings. Users then choose which pages to share during consent.

Agent use caseScopesWhat it costs you
Read pages and databasesRead contentOn by default
Edit pages and database entriesUpdate contentOn by default
Create pages and entriesInsert contentOn by default
Read or add commentsRead commentsInsert commentsOff by default
Read people and emailsRead user information including email addressesDefault option; narrow it if you don't need emails
Minimal set: "Answer questions from docs" agentRead contentNo user information
Turn off update and insert, and pick "No user information".

Changing scopes later

  • Capabilities can be edited on the connection page.
  • Page access is per user: users must re-share pages if your agent needs new ones.
  • No review is triggered by capability changes.

OAuth
None

Build and test

First customers
Same connection.

Scale
Same connection, optional Marketplace listing.

Empty results are the top support issueUsers pick pages during consent. If they share nothing, your agent sees nothing. Tell users in your product which pages to share. Official docs

  • Defaults are broad. New connections can read user email addresses unless you change it.

OAuth app readiness guide · Messaging

Getting your Slack app ready for real users

Tested in a real setup attemptChecked 2026-10-28slack.com

Verdict. You can have a Slack app installable in any workspace in under 10 minutes, with no review. But if your agent reads channel or thread history, that is throttled to 1 request a minute until Slack approves a Marketplace listing, which takes up to about 12 weeks after you reach 10 active workspaces.

01

At a glance

The answer in one screen
Ease of creation
Easy
About 5 minutes from a manifest. Measured in our test.
Ease of approval
Hard
Marketplace review, gated by 10 active workspaces.
Your hands-on time
10 min to 2 days
10 minutes to a working app. 1 to 2 days to prepare a Marketplace submission.
Waiting on the provider
None, or ~12 weeks
None to go live. Up to 10 business days plus up to 10 weeks for Marketplace review.
Do you need your own app yet?
Not to start. Composio has a managed Slack app.
Move to your own app when you need your brand on the consent screen, scopes beyond Composio's defaults, or your own rate limits instead of a shared quota.
Watch out: decisions you can't undo
  • The workspace that owns the app is permanent. Create the app in a workspace your company owns and will keep, never in a personal or trial workspace.
  • Turning distribution off later uninstalls you everywhere. Treat "Activate Public Distribution" as a one-way door once customers are on it.
  • A Marketplace listing locks the app. Request every scope you will need in the next 6 to 12 months before you submit, and keep a separate staging app.
  • Token rotation changes how you must store tokens. Decide before launch. If you turn it on, store the newest refresh token every time, or connections die with invalid_grant.
Agent an agent can do it You needs you Waiting on the provider
02

Prerequisites

What to have ready

To create and connect

  • A company-owned Slack workspace to own the app
  • A second workspace to test installs as a customer would
  • An HTTPS redirect URL. For Composio, the callback shown in your auth config
  • No hard-coded tokens or webhook URLs in your code (you attest to this)

For approval (can take days)

  • 10 or more active workspaces (used in the last 28 days). The counter updates every 24 hours
  • Public homepage, privacy policy, support contact
  • Demo video: install, OAuth, setup, real use, uninstall
  • Test credentials and dummy data for your own product
03

App types

Which one is right for an agent product?

Single-workspace

The default after you create an app.
Who can install
Only the workspace it was built in
Review
None
Use it for
Building and testing
Recommended for agents

Distributed (unlisted)

After "Activate Public Distribution".
Who can install
Any workspace, through your install link
Review
None. Took effect instantly in our test.
Use it for
Beta and first customers

Marketplace (listed)

After Slack approves your submission.
Who can install
Anyone, and discoverable in Slack
Review
Yes, up to about 12 weeks
Use it for
Commercial product at scale
"Stay unlisted forever" is not a real option for a paid product.Slack's API terms say an app that is monetized, or connects to a paid product, needs Slack's authorization to be distributed commercially. For most apps that means the Marketplace; a partner agreement is the alternative. Apps built for one specific customer are exempt. Official docs
Recommended path for an agentBuild single-workspace, activate distribution for beta, and plan the Marketplace from day one if your agent reads messages. Slack's console now also offers an "AI agent" app template and an Agents settings page. Tested
04

Creation steps

Who does what, and how long it takes
  1. YouSign in at api.slack.com/apps
    1 min
    The agent cannot sign in for you. Use the company-owned workspace (decision 1).
  2. AgentCreate New App, choose "From a manifest"
    1 min
    The dialog also offers AI agent, Starter app and Blank app templates. A manifest is faster and reviewable.
  3. AgentWrite the manifest
    2 min
    App name, bot user, scopes from section 4, the HTTPS redirect URL, and token_rotation_enabled set deliberately.
  4. YouApprove "Create and Install"
    10 sec
    Creating and installing into your workspace is now a single step. Settings open at app.slack.com/app-settings.
  5. YouCopy Client ID and Secret into Composio
    2 min
    Create a custom auth config and pass its ID for the slack toolkit. See section 11 on keeping the secret out of sight.
  6. AgentClear the distribution checklist
    1 min
    With a manifest, 3 of 4 items pass automatically. The last is a checkbox confirming no hard-coded tokens.
  7. YouApprove "Activate Public Distribution"
    5 sec
    No review. Took effect instantly. Without it, other workspaces get invalid_team_for_non_distributed_app.
  8. YouTest install from a second workspace
    10 min
    Use an incognito window, as a new customer would.

Total in our test: about 5 minutes of agent work, one sign-in and two approvals.

05

Scopes

What each permission costs you

Agents usually use bot scopes (the app acts as itself, token starts xoxb-). User scopes act as the person (xoxp-) and are needed for things like search.

Agent use caseScopesWhat it costs you
Post messageschat:writeNo limit
List channels and peoplechannels:readusers:readNo limit
Read user emailsusers:read.emailNo limit
Read public channel historychannels:history1 req/min, 15 messages per call until listed
Read private channels and DMsgroups:historyim:history1 req/min, 15 messages per call until listed
Read threadschannels:historySame throttle via conversations.replies
Minimal set: "Post updates" agentchat:writechannels:read
No review pressure at all.
Minimal set: "Summarize my channels" agentchat:writechannels:readchannels:history
Hits the history throttle immediately. See section 8.

Changing scopes later

  • While unlisted: add scopes freely in the manifest, but every existing workspace must reinstall to grant them. Existing connections do not upgrade on their own.
  • Once listed: a new scope needs resubmission with a demo video and a staging app.
  • In Composio: the scopes your auth config requests must match what the app allows, then users reconnect.
06

Approval and distribution

Review, cost and renewal

When you need it: To lift the history throttle, and for commercial distribution under Slack's terms. Cost: None from Slack. Renewal: None, but listed apps are locked (decision 3).

Gate
10 workspaces
Active in the last 28 days, before you can submit.
Step 1
Automated checks
Run in the console before submitting.
Step 2
Up to 10 business days
Preliminary review of listing and scopes. Resubmitting resets your place in the queue.
Step 3
Up to 10 weeks
Functional review: a reviewer installs and tests. Queue place is kept.

What you submit

  • Listing content and scope justifications
  • Security and compliance answers
  • Testing information and credentials
  • Demo video (install to uninstall)

Common rejection reasons

  • Broad or legacy scopes
  • Scopes for features that do not exist yet
  • Reviewer cannot install the app
  • Coded workflows (not eligible)

Slack will not speed up review for a launch date. Submit early.

Before approval: what works and what's capped

Build and test
Your own workspace only.
Limit: Other workspaces cannot install until distribution is active.
First customers
Any workspace can install, no review.
Limit: History and thread reads: 1 request/min, 15 messages per call.
Scale
Marketplace listing approved.
Limit: Standard rate-limit tiers. Changes need re-review.
What this means for an agentReading the last 200 messages of one busy channel takes about 14 minutes. Until you are listed, design around events (subscribe to new messages as they arrive) instead of polling history. Internal (customer-built) apps keep 50+ requests/min and 1,000 objects. Official docs
07

Data use and compliance

Rules that shape agent design
  • No LLM training on data from Slack APIs, for apps used outside the installing organization.
  • No bulk export of messages and files without a separate agreement.
  • Keep only what you need. Use, processing and retention must be the minimum the app needs to run.
  • No persistent copies or indexes of other organizations' data via the Data Access and Real-time Search APIs. Brief caching only.
Design impact"Sync the whole workspace into a vector database" is ruled out for a distributed app. Query live, cache briefly. Official docs
08

Common blockers

Symptom, cause, fix
SymptomCauseFix
invalid_team_for_non_distributed_appDistribution not activatedManage Distribution, then Activate Public Distribution
redirect_uri mismatchURL differs from the registered one, or is not HTTPSCopy the exact callback from your Composio auth config
History calls return 15 messages and get rate limitedUnlisted app throttleUse events, or go through Marketplace review
invalid_grant on refreshRotation on, an old refresh token was reusedStore the newest refresh token every time
Agent missing new permissionsScopes added but workspaces did not reinstallAsk users to reconnect; check granted scopes
Customer cannot install in their company workspaceTheir admin requires app approvalGive customers an admin-approval note Not verified
